t:
(a) In General.—Chapter 21 of title 36, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section:“§ 2115. Acquisition, operation, and maintenance of Lafayette Escadrille Memorial  “The American Battle Monuments Commission may enter into an agreement with the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation to acquire, operate, and maintain the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in Marnes-la-Coquette, France. Under such an agreement, the Commission shall make necessary arrangements to ensure the ongoing maintenance of the memorial, including the cemetery at the memorial that contains the remains of 49 aviators of the United States who died during World War I.”
. 
    (b) Clerical Amendment.—The table of sections at the beginning of chapter 21 of such title is amended by adding at the end of the following new item:

“2115. 
Acquisition, operation, and maintenance of Lafayette Escadrille Memorial.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that an agreement with a private foundation counts as coordination with an outside entity. But this is a transactional arrangement to acquire and maintain a memorial, not a process that gives outsiders a say in a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation requirement, or right to sue. The rest of the section is a clerical amendment.
fable.s: The American Battle Monuments Commission may enter into an agreement with the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation to acquire, operate, and maintain the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in Marnes-la-Coquette, France.

opus.w: This section lets a federal commission make a property and maintenance agreement with a private foundation. That is a deal between the two parties, which the definition excludes along with contracts. It does not set up any consultation, advisory body, hearing, comment period or right to sue. The Foundation sits outside the federal government, but it is a party to a deal, not a participant in a federal policy decision.
opus.s: The American Battle Monuments Commission may enter into an agreement with the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation to acquire, operate, and maintain the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in Marnes-la-Coquette, France.
opus.b: The tempting reading is "Yes," because the Commission makes an agreement with an outside party, the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation. But that agreement is a deal to transfer and look after property. It is not a process where the Foundation is consulted or advises on a federal decision, and the definition leaves out contracts.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes a federal agency to enter into a contractual agreement with a non-profit organization to perform specific tasks (acquisition, operation, maintenance). This falls under the exclusion for contracts or cooperative agreements, not participation in decision-making. The outside party is executing a service, not consulting on or advising a federal policy decision.
qwen_chat.s: The American Battle Monuments Commission may enter into an agreement with the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation to acquire, operate, and maintain the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial in Marnes-la-Coquette, France.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that entering into an agreement with the Lafayette Escadrille Memorial Foundation (a non-profit organization outside the federal government) constitutes "coordination" or "consultation" with an outside party. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits, grants, contracts, or licenses" are not participation. An agreement to acquire, operate, and maintain a memorial is essentially a contract or cooperative arrangement for service delivery, not a process where the outside party participates in a federal decision-making process (like an advisory board or public comment period). The outside entity is a partner in execution, not a participant in the decision.
